recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-3484 unless a future Pharmacy decision changes the type or semantics of MedicationDispense.daysSupply.
issue_request: FHIR-3484 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Pharmacy change request noting that MedicationDispense documentation mentioned days supply but the model lacked a corresponding days supply field, unlike MedicationPrescription.dispense.expectedSupplyDuration.
initial_application: No FHIR-3484-tagged commit was found. The requested change appears to have been applied implicitly by the 2015 Pharmacy update commit abce09d8c1edffa07e8bd6fbdf60eaa097da3d91, which added MedicationDispense.daysSupply to the old MedicationDispense spreadsheet source; the 2021 source rework retained the element in the current StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: MedicationDispense is active in source/fhir.ini. The current source defines MedicationDispense.daysSupply as 0..1 SimpleQuantity, and MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.expectedSupplyDuration remains present for the prescription-side parallel called out by the issue. Searches found only separate background items: FHIR-5165 on Quantity comparator policy and FHIR-45153 on a later fillNumber element after daysSupply.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current FHIR-core source already satisfies the requested days-supply capture capability.

related_jiras.note: Separate Published datatypes/Quantity comparator issue; comments mention MedicationDispense.daysSupply only as one of many Quantity uses and do not reopen the FHIR-3484 field-existence decision.
